text: Meanwhile, back at the VitaminAir Community in Cambodia  ...
Jonathan and I at his home in Torrance, California. Jonathan is an emergency room doctor.

It's been 3 months since landing in the US, and that time has been spent camping and exploring places and opportunities along a 100 mile stretch of the southern California coast, from Santa Barbara County to Los Angeles County. 

Today,  after filing some papers at the Los Angeles Superior Court in Santa Monica, I will begin journeying further south, to San Diego County, and from there I will cross over the mountains to the desert and into Imperial Valley.

Above photo - nearing sunset, and Sunset Boulevard, looking toward Los Angeles,  Saturday October 16th.

Highway traffic into Los Angeles from points north, very heavy and congested. 

I have begun my journey to the east. You are welcome to follow along. Direct message me with comments and questions. 
.

Entrance to Camp Pendleton, from San Clemente I would say one of the nicest stretches of bikepaths along the southern California coast.
Very enjoyable weather, scenery, and infrastructure. I imagine San Clemente to be a nice place to live if one prefers to live along the southern California coast.
Then you come to Oceanside, which is where I begin my trip east, to the inland.
Eastbound ‐ have left the Pacific Coast for good, at least for this trip.

The programming for this bicycle storage box is quite good, simple, and worth copying.

www.bikelink.org
Posted on a community bulletin board at San Ysabel, a small community near Julian, California. It's quite an ideal little rural mountain community in eastern San Diego County.

Coffee and view at the county park in Julian California. In this remote community I would consider settling down, but I have yet to fully explore the area.

Right now I'm at the Julian Public library using the free wifi.

The photos above were taken at skateboarding are of the county park. The library is very nearby.

https://www.google.com/search?q=Julian+California+scenery+&tbm=isch

Some photos of the area.  It's a much better, more sane and safe world than along the coast.

Wonderful California weather and all the  benefits San Diego County offers.

They've changed the American flag, or at least some people have.  American people are more divided than ever, but actually everyone behaves quite civil, unless you happen to say the wrong thing to the wrong person.

Julian is a historic gold mining town, that is now a popular tourist destination for coastal city folks who regularly invade the place to spend money at the restaurants. The surrounding rural areas are the best feature, while the local townspeople are friendly and talkative when they're not busy serving the tourists. 

The town itself, and even the whole area is very hill, not suitable for bicycle touring. It requires super human strength to cycle here from the coast. Most all the hills I needed to walk up them.
Posted on the local bulletin board

On the edge of Julian, toward Brawley, my next major stop.  It will be mostly downhill from here to sea level.  Julian is at 4000 plus feet above sea level, so it's been a long two day climb to get here from the coast.

Now I will descend into the Imperial Valley and the Salton Sea, which is where Brawley is located. There are some hot springs down there I want to visit.
From Julian to Brawley, mostly all downhill. Three to four hours?

Many homeless living just this way in this small desert town.  Not a lot, but many, a much greater percentage than you would find in other small towns across America. 

It's not for lack of food or clothing, but of shelter. Places of dignity where they can live, and experience a good night's sleep.

Brawley is located in the Colorado Desert and Lower Colorado River Valley regions. 

The city's elevation, like other Imperial Valley towns, is below sea level.

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brawley,_California

A more elaborate homeless encampment located about 4 miles east of town center along the Alamo River, whose source is located in Mexico .  It is not a clean river, and it flows northerly into the Salton Sea.

Salton Sea area is a very special place, mainly because it's different, nowhere else in the world like it.

California was hit by a historic record rain and snowfall these past few days.

If I were still along the coast, life would be miserably cold and wet.

Fortunately, I crossed the mountain into Imperial Valley just at the right time to enjoy the lovely weather we're having here. 

Last night there was even a bit of rain here, but the temperatures both day and night are lovely, dry, very comfortable in the shade, and being in the hot autumn sun is nice too.
A lovely old tractor worth preserving. It sits upon land along the Alamo River that is for sale. Several more old antiques to be found on this site.
The whole place is for sale if anyone wants it.

The land is at the corner of Rt 78 and the Alamo river 4 miles east of Brawley. The homeless encampment photo above is beneath the bridge on the left (west) side.

Many interesting artifacts remain on this land. 

32.97904° N, 115.46677° W
.

Some overhead views of Imperial Valley. I am situated in Brawley, the only major population center at the south end of the Salton Sea. 

Further south, you can see the satellite image of how the US and Mexico meet at the border. Most all of this Valley is at or below sea level.

The two river systems flowing north into the Salton Sea from Mexico are very polluted,  but from a distance overlook, they can be quite majestic.

Two new additions to the "what to carry and why" list for the vagabond traveler. 

A short water hose to screw onto an ordinary water tap, and a "key" to turn on those taps that don't have a handle. 

Buckets, or something to use as a bucket, such as a big plastic jug with the top cut off, are easy enough to find on the fly.

This combination works well for bathing, laundry, and occasionally spraying clean a dirty oily bicycle chain and cluster.

Can't think of a more practical place to store the water hose, and it's just about the right length. 

At this location in Brawley, the "Cattle Call Park", I have easy access to electricity as well as water.

So far, full access wifi is the most difficult service to acquire, as so many vendors are blocking and filtering data ports.
